title: Undercut and Rally
teaches: The undercut and rally as we trade it: a leader dips a few cents to a few percent under a level everyone can see, then takes it back within three sessions. We buy with a market order as price trades back over the level, never the undercut itself. The stop sits a few cents under the undercut low, a third comes off at 3R and 5R, and a loss at the stop is the plan working.

facts.quote: Once the stock undercuts a prior low in the pattern and rallies back above it, a long entry is generated at the prior low which is then used as a selling guide.
facts.claim: Morales: once the stock undercuts a prior low and rallies back above it, a long entry is generated at that low, which becomes the selling guide.

facts.quote: Volume is generally not a factor, and often the best U&R set-ups in individual stocks occur in conjunction with a market turn to the upside after a period of correcting.
facts.claim: Morales: the best U&Rs often come with a market turn to the upside after a correction.

facts.quote: where a stock undercuts a prior low in the pattern, usually along the lows of a potential new base, and then rallies back above that low, triggering a buy signal based on the U&R.
facts.claim: Morales and Kacher: a U&R undercuts a prior low, usually along the lows of a potential new base, then rallies back above it.

facts.quote: When a leading stock breaks below its moving average, a move back above the moving average can provide a long entry point as the stock moves back up through the line.
facts.claim: Morales and Kacher: a leading stock that breaks below its moving average and moves back up through it gives a long entry.

facts.quote: essentially undercuts the moving average, faking out sellers and would-be short-sellers, and then rallies back above it.
facts.claim: Morales and Kacher: the MAU&R undercuts the average, fakes out sellers and would-be short-sellers, then rallies back above.

facts.quote: Once the buy signal is triggered, one then uses the moving average as a selling guide, and can adjust their stop to 1-2% below the line depending on risk-preference.
facts.claim: Morales and Kacher: after the MAU&R buy, the stop can sit 1-2% below the moving average line.

facts.quote: If the buy-stop is filled, immediately place an initial (Good Till Cancelled) stop just below today's low.
facts.claim: Turtle Soup (via StockCharts): after the fill, place the initial stop just below today's low.

facts.quote: After the market falls below the prior 20-day low, place an entry buy-stop slightly above the previous 20-day low.
facts.claim: Turtle Soup (via StockCharts): the buy-stop sits slightly above the previous 20-day low, after price has fallen under it.

facts.quote: a spring is a price move below the support level of the TR (established in Phases A and B) that quickly reverses and moves back into the TR.
facts.claim: Wyckoff: a spring is a move below the range's support that quickly reverses back into the range.

facts.quote: Shakeouts may also occur once a price advance has started, with rapid downward movement intended to induce retail traders and investors in long positions to sell their shares to large operators.
facts.claim: Wyckoff: a shakeout is a rapid drop meant to induce holders to sell to large operators.

facts.quote: As with a double bottom, the shakeout-plus-three pattern has two lows, with the second low undercutting the first.
facts.claim: IBD: the shakeout-plus-three has two lows, the second undercutting the first.

facts.quote: Add three points to the price of the first low.
facts.claim: IBD: the shakeout-plus-three buy point is three points over the first low.

facts.quote: Candlestick pattern formed when the price undercuts below the previous day's low, but then closes above the previous day's close.
facts.claim: Deepvue: a bullish reversal bar undercuts the previous day's low and closes above the previous close.

facts.quote: Stop first (by default a few cents under the day's low or the prior day's low, F62); the size comes from the stop; if the honest stop does not fit the risk, skip the trade.
facts.claim: A3: stop first, a few cents under the day's low; the size comes from the stop; if the honest stop does not fit, skip.

facts.claim: A4: the stop is the exit; it only moves up, never wider; the gap rule is the one exception.

walkthroughs.title: QCOM, September 2020: the same-day trap
steps: QCOM, 2020. A two-week flat shelf on the 50-day. The level to watch is 109.62, set on 09-08.
2020-09-21: the low hits 108.30, 1.20% under the level, and price is back over 109.62 the same day.
Buy at market as it clears the level, 109.63. Stop a few cents under the undercut low, 108.25: 1.26% away.
Failure mode: a close back under the level, then the low breaks. Instead 3R came in 1 day; it ran to 37.3R.

walkthroughs.title: WYNN, November 2013: two closes under, then a gap back
steps: WYNN, 2013. The level is 159.37, set on 11-07. The stock closes under it two days running.
2013-11-21: it gaps back over 159.37. The undercut low was 157.48, 1.19% under. The reclaim came inside the window.
Buy at market at the open, 159.97, 0.4% over the level. Stop under the undercut low: 157.43, 1.59% away.
Failure mode: the reclaim fails and 157.43 breaks. Instead 3R took 8 days. Slow, and it ran to 26.0R.

walkthroughs.title: NVDA, April 2024: a planned loss
steps: NVDA, 2024. The level is 87.62, set on 04-02. One close under it, a 1.99% undercut. It reclaims the next day.
2024-04-05: buy at market as it clears the level, 87.63. Stop a few cents under the undercut low: 85.83, 2.05% away.
Failure mode, and it happened: 0.67R, then a low of 83.02 on 04-09. The stop was the exit.
A planned loss. Even the best-looking reclaim loses about 58% of the time. A new try needs a new trigger.

questions.q: In one line, what is an undercut and rally?
choices: A dip under a low, then a quick reclaim
A breakout over a flat ceiling
A slow drift under the 200-day
A gap up on earnings news
questions.answer: A dip under a low, then a quick reclaim
questions.why: A dip under a low, then a quick reclaim. Morales: the stock undercuts a prior low and rallies back above it.
questions.lesson_line: A U&R is a trap: the stock breaks a low everyone sees, then takes it right back.

wrong.A breakout over a flat ceiling: That is a flat base breakout. A U&R breaks a low first, then takes it back.
wrong.A slow drift under the 200-day: A slow drift is no trap. A U&R is a fast dip and reclaim, and we do not buy under the 200-day.
wrong.A gap up on earnings news: A gap up is an earnings or news setup. A U&R starts with a break of a low.

questions.q: In Morales's U&R, the long entry is generated at the prior low as the stock rallies back above it.
questions.answer: True
questions.why: True. His entry comes at the prior low once the stock rallies back above it, and that low then becomes the selling guide.
questions.lesson_line: The entry is the way back up through the low, not the way down.

questions.q: We buy the undercut itself, before the level is back, to get a better price.
questions.answer: False
questions.why: False. Never buy the undercut itself before the level is back. Turtle Soup also waits for a buy-stop just above the broken low.
questions.lesson_line: A better price under the level is a guess. Wait for the way back.

questions.q: Tap the word that fits the blank.
questions.sentence: The undercut low is the ___ low while price was under the level.
questions.answer: lowest
questions.why: Lowest. The undercut low is the lowest low while price was under the level, and the stop goes a few cents under it.
questions.lesson_line: Find the lowest low under the level. That is the price the stop protects.

questions.q: When does a U&R buy trigger?
choices: As price trades back above the level
As price first trades under the level
At the close of the third day under it
When it makes a new 52-week high
questions.answer: As price trades back above the level
questions.why: As price trades back above the level. The undercut is the trap; the way back up through the level is the trigger.
questions.lesson_line: Buy the reclaim, not the dip.

wrong.As price first trades under the level: That is the undercut itself. Never buy it before the level is back.
wrong.At the close of the third day under it: Three days under is the edge of the window. It is a limit, not a signal.
wrong.When it makes a new 52-week high: A new high is a different setup. The U&R buys the reclaim of the level.

questions.q: How do we place a U&R entry order?
choices: A market order as it clears the level
A limit order under the undercut low
A stop order at last week's high
A limit order at the 50-day
questions.answer: A market order as it clears the level
questions.why: A market order as it clears the level. Entries are market orders, and the stop goes in with the buy.
questions.lesson_line: Market order on the reclaim. The stop goes in the same minute.

wrong.A limit order under the undercut low: That waits for the break to get worse. It buys the undercut, not the reclaim.
wrong.A stop order at last week's high: That is a later, higher entry. The U&R buys as price trades back over the level.
wrong.A limit order at the 50-day: A limit at an average can sit unfilled while the stock leaves. Entries are market orders.

questions.q: The level in a U&R should be a price that many traders can see.
questions.answer: True
questions.why: True. The undercut works because a level everyone can see fakes out sellers and would-be short-sellers.
questions.lesson_line: A trap needs a crowd. Pick a level everyone can see.

questions.q: After the buy, what is the exit?
choices: A trade under the undercut low
A close under the 10-day average
The next red day
A new low in the index
questions.answer: A trade under the undercut low
questions.why: A trade under the undercut low. It proves the trap wrong, and the stop is the exit.
questions.lesson_line: Under the undercut low, you are out. No second thoughts.

wrong.A close under the 10-day average: That trails the last third after the trims. The first exit is the stop.
wrong.The next red day: One red day is noise. The stop was set before the buy.
wrong.A new low in the index: The index is context. The stop is on the stock.

questions.q: Tap the word that fits the blank.
questions.sentence: No close back above the level within ___ sessions means a breakdown, not a U&R.
questions.why: 3. With no close back above the level within 3 sessions, it is a breakdown and there is no trade.
questions.lesson_line: Three sessions to take it back. After that it is a breakdown.

questions.q: A stock closes under its level for 8 sessions, then retakes it. That is a U&R.
questions.answer: False
questions.why: False. No close back above the level within 3 sessions is a breakdown. 5 or more closes under is a Remount, a different setup.
questions.lesson_line: A long stay under a line is a Remount, not a U&R.

questions.q: When does a U&R tend to work best?
choices: After a correction, as markets turn up
Late in a long, extended rally
While the index keeps making lower lows
Only in the first hour of trading
questions.answer: After a correction, as markets turn up
questions.why: After a correction, as markets turn up. Morales: the best ones often come with a market turn to the upside after a correction.
questions.lesson_line: Best after a correction, when the market itself turns up.

wrong.Late in a long, extended rally: Morales ties the best ones to a turn after a correction, not to the end of a long run.
wrong.While the index keeps making lower lows: A falling index is how correct-looking U&Rs get stopped. The turn comes first.
wrong.Only in the first hour of trading: Time of day is not the condition. The market turn is.

questions.q: A $6 stock that trades $50 million a day passes our price and volume rule for a U&R.
questions.answer: False
questions.why: False. We trade only stocks at $10 or more that trade at least $20 million a day. The volume passes and the price fails.
questions.lesson_line: Ten dollars and twenty million a day. Both, every time.

questions.q: Who does the undercut fool?
choices: Sellers and would-be short-sellers
Only long-term holders
Only market makers
Nobody; it is only a dip
questions.answer: Sellers and would-be short-sellers
questions.why: Sellers and would-be short-sellers. The break looks bearish, then price rallies back above it and they are caught.
questions.lesson_line: The undercut shakes out sellers. The reclaim traps the shorts.

wrong.Only long-term holders: The break scares holders into selling, but the trap also catches shorts who pile on.
wrong.Only market makers: The crowd that trades the visible level is the target, not one desk.
wrong.Nobody; it is only a dip: A dip nobody trades is no trap. The U&R works because the break draws sellers and shorts in.

questions.q: How many closes under the level separate a U&R from a Remount?
choices: Up to 3 is a U&R; 5 or more is a Remount
Up to 10 is a U&R; 15 or more, Remount
Any number is a U&R if it reclaims
One is a U&R; two or more is a Remount
questions.answer: Up to 3 is a U&R; 5 or more is a Remount
questions.why: Up to 3 closes under then back above is a U&R. 5 or more closes under the line is a Remount.
questions.lesson_line: Count the closes under the level. Three or fewer is a U&R.

wrong.Up to 10 is a U&R; 15 or more, Remount: Ten closes under a level is a long stay, a Remount. A U&R is brief.
wrong.Any number is a U&R if it reclaims: The stay matters. A long stay under a line is a Remount, a separate setup.
wrong.One is a U&R; two or more is a Remount: Two or three closes under still fit a U&R. The Remount starts at 5.

questions.q: Where does the U&R stop go?
choices: A few cents under the undercut low
A few cents under the level
1% under the 50-day
Under the base low
questions.answer: A few cents under the undercut low
questions.why: A few cents under the undercut low. Turtle Soup puts its stop just below today's low too: the low of the break is the line.
questions.lesson_line: Stop first: a few cents under the undercut low.

wrong.A few cents under the level: Price already traded under the level once. The undercut low is what proves the trap wrong.
wrong.1% under the 50-day: That is a stop for a different idea. This one hangs on the undercut low.
wrong.Under the base low: The base low can sit far away. The stop is the undercut low, which keeps it near the buy.

questions.q: A close back under the level after the buy means sell at that close.
questions.answer: False
questions.why: False. A close back under the level is the early warning, not the exit. Hold to the stop and do not add.
questions.lesson_line: A warning, not an exit. The stop decides, and you never add.

questions.q: The level is 59.95 and the undercut low is 59.04. How far under the level, in percent?
questions.why: 1.5%. The level minus the undercut low, divided by the level. STLD's undercut was 1.52%, a shallow dip.
questions.lesson_line: Measure the dip: level minus the low, over the level.

questions.q: A moving average undercut and rally uses the average as the level.
questions.answer: True
questions.why: True. Morales and Kacher: a leading stock breaks below its moving average, then moves back up through it for a long entry.
questions.lesson_line: A MAU&R is the same trap, with an average as the level.

questions.q: In Morales's words, which kind of level does a U&R undercut?
choices: A prior low in the pattern
The prior day's high
The all-time high
The 52-week low only
questions.answer: A prior low in the pattern
questions.why: A prior low in the pattern. Both Morales sources say a U&R undercuts a prior low and rallies back above it.
questions.lesson_line: Undercut a prior low, then take it back.

wrong.The prior day's high: An undercut goes under a low, not a high.
wrong.The all-time high: A U&R breaks a low and takes it back. A high is not an undercut level.
wrong.The 52-week low only: Morales names a prior low in the pattern, usually along a potential new base. It need not be a 52-week low.

questions.q: Buy the reclaim?
choices: No, a report inside 3 sessions
Yes, the shape is perfect
Yes, at half size
Yes, buyout news lifts it
questions.answer: No, a report inside 3 sessions
questions.why: No. No new buys when a report is inside 3 sessions, and a pending buyout or deal is a no as well.
questions.lesson_line: Report inside 3 sessions or a deal pending: no new buy.

wrong.Yes, the shape is perfect: The shape passes. The calendar and the headline do not.
wrong.Yes, at half size: Half size is still a new buy inside the window. The rule is a hard line.
wrong.Yes, buyout news lifts it: Pending buyout or deal news takes the name off the list.

questions.story: A clean U&R of the 40.00 level triggers at 10:05. The company reports earnings in two sessions. A buyout headline hit this morning.

questions.q: What do you do?
choices: Wait for a trade back above 170.00
Buy now, it is cheap
Buy half now, half on the reclaim
Buy now and set a tight stop
questions.answer: Wait for a trade back above 170.00
questions.why: Wait. Never buy the undercut itself before the level is back; if it never comes back, there is no trade.
questions.lesson_line: No reclaim, no trade. Let the level come back first.

wrong.Buy now, it is cheap: Cheap is the trap. If the level never comes back there is no trade.
wrong.Buy half now, half on the reclaim: The first half is the undercut itself. One price, one stop, and no adding.
wrong.Buy now and set a tight stop: A tight stop does not fix a buy made before the level is back.

questions.story: The stock is 2% under the 170.00 level at 10:05. It has not come back through.

questions.q: Fill 60.18. The undercut low is 59.04 and the stop sits five cents under it. How far below the fill, in percent?
questions.why: 1.98%. The stop is a few cents under the undercut low, and well inside the 3% the stop usually sits within. That was STLD.
questions.lesson_line: Stop first, then the distance. Under 3% fits.

questions.q: Bought at 135.38 with the stop at 133.69. Where is 3R?
questions.why: 140.45. One R is the fill minus the stop. Add three of those to the fill. The first third comes off there.
questions.lesson_line: Know your 3R before the open. A third comes off there.

questions.q: If the undercut low breaks by a few cents, widen the stop so the trade can breathe.
questions.answer: False
questions.why: False. The stop is the exit. It only moves up, never down or wider. The gap rule is the one exception.
questions.lesson_line: The stop only moves up. Never wider.

questions.q: Tap the word that fits the blank.
questions.sentence: On one stock, at most 3 tries a week and ___ a month.
questions.why: 6. A new try only on a new trigger, at most 3 a week and 6 a month on one stock.
questions.lesson_line: Three a week, six a month on one stock, each on a new trigger.

questions.q: Tap the word that fits the blank.
questions.sentence: A third comes off at ___R and another third at 5R, then the rest trails.
questions.why: 3. The hard rule is a third at 3R, another third at 5R, then trail the last third.
questions.lesson_line: A third at 3R, a third at 5R, trail the rest.

questions.q: What now?
choices: Hold; the stop is still the exit
Sell at the close, the trap failed
Widen the stop to give it room
Add on the dip
questions.answer: Hold; the stop is still the exit
questions.why: Hold it. A close back under the level is the early warning, not the exit. Hold to the stop and do not add.
questions.lesson_line: A weak close is a warning. Hold to the stop, never add.

wrong.Sell at the close, the trap failed: A close back under the level is a warning. The stop was set before the buy, and it decides.
wrong.Widen the stop to give it room: The stop only moves up, never wider.
wrong.Add on the dip: Full size at one price with one stop. We do not add to a trap that is failing.

questions.story: You bought the reclaim of 141.00 at 141.20 with the stop at 138.90. The day closes at 139.80, back under the level, above your stop.

questions.q: The level is 50.00. The stock trades at 52.30. How far over the level, in percent?
questions.why: 4.6%. That is more than 4% over the level, so we pass. Chasing costs size, not risk.
questions.lesson_line: Four percent over the level and I am done. Pass.

questions.q: Bought at 111.65, stop 110.18. The stock trades to 119.00. How many R is that?
questions.why: 5R. Each R is the fill minus the stop. That is where the second third comes off. VEEV reached 3R in a day.
questions.lesson_line: Count in R, not dollars. 5R is the second trim.

questions.q: Where does the stop go?
choices: A few cents under 46.90
A few cents under 47.40
A few cents under 48.00
Under day three's low
questions.answer: A few cents under 46.90
questions.why: A few cents under 46.90. The undercut low is the lowest low while price was under the level.
questions.lesson_line: The stop hides under the lowest low of the whole dip.

wrong.A few cents under 47.40: Day two traded lower. The undercut low is the lowest low while price was under the level.
wrong.A few cents under 48.00: The level was lost for two days. The stop sits under the undercut low.
wrong.Under day three's low: Day three is the reclaim. A trade back under the undercut low is what ends the idea.

questions.story: A stock closes under its 48.00 level two days running. Day one's low is 47.40. Day two's low is 46.90. On day three it gaps back over 48.00.

questions.q: What trails the last third of a fast mover?
choices: A close under the 10-day average
A close under the 200-day
A new 5-day low
A trade under the undercut low
questions.answer: A close under the 10-day average
questions.why: A close under the 10-day average. The 21-day suits a steadier mover; sell on a close below it.
questions.lesson_line: Fast mover, 10-day. Steadier, 21-day. Sell on a close under.

wrong.A close under the 200-day: That is far too slow for a fast mover. The 21-day suits a steadier one.
wrong.A new 5-day low: A short-term low is not our trail. We use the 10-day or the 21-day average.
wrong.A trade under the undercut low: That is the first stop. After the trims it moves up and the trail takes over.

questions.q: What now?
choices: Sell; under 1R after 10 sessions
Hold; the stop is not hit
Add to the position
Move the stop to breakeven
questions.answer: Sell; under 1R after 10 sessions
questions.why: Sell. A trade still under 1R after 10 trading days is sold, which frees the money.
questions.lesson_line: Ten sessions, under 1R: out.

wrong.Hold; the stop is not hit: The stop is not the only exit. A trade still under 1R after 10 sessions is sold.
wrong.Add to the position: We do not add. The money is better used on a new setup.
wrong.Move the stop to breakeven: Breakeven comes at 2R to 5R, not at 0.4R.

questions.story: Ten sessions after the buy, the stock sits at 0.4R. The stop has not been hit and no trim has come off.

questions.q: What do you do?
choices: Get out; that low is past 2R
Set the stop at 131.20 and hold
Keep the 133.69 stop and wait
Buy more at the lower price
questions.answer: Get out; that low is past 2R
questions.why: Get out. A gap through the stop hands it to the first 30-minute low, but if that takes the loss past 2R, get out.
questions.lesson_line: The first 30 minutes decide. Past 2R, you are out.

wrong.Set the stop at 131.20 and hold: The first 30-minute low is the new stop, but only up to a ceiling. Past 2R, you are out.
wrong.Keep the 133.69 stop and wait: The stock is already through it. The gap rule hands the stop to the first 30 minutes.
wrong.Buy more at the lower price: No adding, and never to a gap against the stop.

questions.story: You bought at 135.38 with the stop at 133.69. Your 1R is 1.69. The next day gaps down to 131.90, and the first 30-minute low is 131.20.

questions.q: What do you do at the open?
choices: Take the first third at the open
Wait for 113.77 on the way down
Hold everything and trail
Sell it all at the open
questions.answer: Take the first third at the open
questions.why: Take the first third at the open. If a stock opens above a trim level, take that trim at the open.
questions.lesson_line: A gap past a trim level: take it at the open.

wrong.Wait for 113.77 on the way down: You may never see it again. A trim level the day opens past is taken at the open.
wrong.Hold everything and trail: The trail is for the last third, after the trims.
wrong.Sell it all at the open: The plan is a third at 3R, a third at 5R, then the trail.

questions.story: You bought at 109.63 with the stop at 108.25. Your 3R level is 113.77. Three days later the stock opens at 115.20.

questions.q: We keep a position under 1% of the stock's average daily volume.
questions.answer: True
questions.why: True. Never own more than 1% of a stock's average daily volume. Thin stocks are not even on the watchlist.
questions.lesson_line: Stay under 1% of daily volume. You must be able to get out.

questions.q: After the first third comes off, where does the stop go?
choices: Up to breakeven, our entry
Up to the reclaimed level
Down, to give it room
It stays until 5R
questions.answer: Up to breakeven, our entry
questions.why: Up to breakeven. The stop goes to breakeven at 2R to 5R, at the first trim by default.
questions.lesson_line: First third off, stop to breakeven.

wrong.Up to the reclaimed level: Raising the stop to the reclaimed level after a day is the journal template's habit, not ours.
wrong.It stays until 5R: Breakeven comes at 2R to 5R, at the first trim by default.

questions.q: Take it or pass?
choices: Pass; the 50-day is falling
Take it; the trap worked
Take it at half size
Wait for the 200-day to turn
questions.answer: Pass; the 50-day is falling
questions.why: Pass. The 50-day must not be falling, and a falling 50-day or price under its averages is normally a pass.
questions.lesson_line: Check the 50-day before the trap. Falling means pass.

wrong.Take it; the trap worked: The trap is only half the check. Under a falling 50-day, the context fails.
wrong.Take it at half size: Smaller size does not turn a falling average into a rising one. It is normally a pass.
wrong.Wait for the 200-day to turn: The 50-day is the line that fails here, so waiting on the 200-day does not fix it.

questions.story: A quick undercut and a reclaim in two sessions. The 50-day is lower than it was 10 sessions ago.

questions.q: On an Orange market reading, a U&R can still be taken if it grades A+.
questions.answer: True
questions.why: True. Orange allows only A+ setups. Green is full risk, Yellow is smaller and fewer, and Red is mostly cash and shorts.
questions.lesson_line: Orange means A+ only. Red means mostly cash.

questions.q: What do you do?
choices: Skip it; Red means mostly cash
Take it; the setup is clean
Take it at full size, it is a leader
Wait for a second reclaim
questions.answer: Skip it; Red means mostly cash
questions.why: Skip it. Red is mostly cash and shorts. ADBE's clean U&R was stopped the day SPY made a lower low.
questions.lesson_line: The market reading beats a pretty chart.

wrong.Take it; the setup is clean: A clean chart does not change the market reading. Correct-looking U&Rs get stopped as the index breaks.
wrong.Take it at full size, it is a leader: Red is mostly cash. Full size is the reading for Green.
wrong.Wait for a second reclaim: A second try needs a new trigger and the reading still decides.

questions.story: A leader makes a textbook U&R of its 20-day. The index broke down yesterday. The market reading is Red.

questions.q: On a MAU&R, where is our stop?
choices: A few cents under the undercut low
1% to 2% under the average
Under the 200-day
At the average itself
questions.answer: A few cents under the undercut low
questions.why: A few cents under the undercut low. VoSI lets the stop sit 1-2% below the line; ours is the low that proves the trap wrong.
questions.lesson_line: Same trap, same stop: under the undercut low.

wrong.1% to 2% under the average: That is Morales and Kacher's guide for the MAU&R. Ours is the undercut low, the price that proves the trap wrong.
wrong.Under the 200-day: The 200-day can be far away. The stop stays near the buy.
wrong.At the average itself: The average was already undercut once. The stop is a few cents under the undercut low.

questions.q: IBD's shakeout-plus-three buys a set number of points over the first low, later than the reclaim.
questions.answer: True
questions.why: True. IBD adds three points to the first low. That is a later, higher entry with a wider stop, and it is not our default.
questions.lesson_line: IBD buys three points over the old low. We buy the reclaim.

questions.q: Write the level, the stop and the size before the open.
questions.answer: True
questions.why: True. The buy waits for the reclaim, but the level, the stop and the size are on paper before the open.
questions.lesson_line: Plan before the open. The market order only executes the plan.

questions.q: The usual way a U&R fails: the reclaim does not hold and the undercut low breaks.
questions.answer: True
questions.why: True. The reclaim fails, then the undercut low breaks, often as the index breaks down. Most hits are stopped.
questions.lesson_line: Most U&Rs get stopped. The few that run pay for them.

questions.q: What is the right read?
choices: A planned loss; wait for a new trigger
Buy back at once, it recovered
A mistake; skip stops next time
Wait for tomorrow and buy the dip
questions.answer: A planned loss; wait for a new trigger
questions.why: A planned loss. The stop is the exit. TRIP closed back above the entry, then fell to 91.78 by 08-01.
questions.lesson_line: The stop that shakes you out is the price of the ones that keep falling.

wrong.Buy back at once, it recovered: After a stop-out, buy again only if the setup triggers again, as a new trade.
wrong.A mistake; skip stops next time: The stop is the exit. TRIP fell on to 91.78 anyway.
wrong.Wait for tomorrow and buy the dip: A dip is not a trigger. A new try needs its own trigger and every rule.

questions.story: Your stop at 100.56 filled when the stock dipped to 100.44. It then closed at 103.35, above your 102.18 entry.

questions.q: U&R or something else?
choices: An Oops, judged on one candle
A U&R of the 10-session low
A Remount
A flat base breakout
questions.answer: An Oops, judged on one candle
questions.why: An Oops. The only level undercut was yesterday's low, so it is judged on one candle. SBUX looked just like this.
questions.lesson_line: Only yesterday's low undercut means an Oops, not a U&R.

wrong.A U&R of the 10-session low: Here the 10-session low is only yesterday's low. A U&R needs a level that matters more than that.
wrong.A Remount: A Remount follows a long stay under a line. This was one day.
wrong.A flat base breakout: There is no base breakout here. This is a one-day undercut and reclaim.

questions.story: The stock opened under its prior close and dipped under yesterday's low. It closed back over yesterday's close. The 10-session low is yesterday's low.

questions.q: Which setup owns this?
choices: A Remount, bought on the retake
A U&R, it reclaimed
An Oops, it undercut a low
Gap Support
questions.answer: A Remount, bought on the retake
questions.why: A Remount. 5 or more closes under the line is a Remount. FDX closed under its level 8 times before the retake.
questions.lesson_line: Eight closes under a line is a Remount, not a U&R.

wrong.A U&R, it reclaimed: Up to 3 closes under is a U&R. Eight is a long stay, so the Remount card applies.
wrong.An Oops, it undercut a low: An Oops is one day of an undercut and reclaim. This stay was far longer.
wrong.Gap Support: Gap Support needs the gap-up day's low as the level. Nothing here says a gap.

questions.story: A leader closed under its 211.18 level for eight sessions in a row. Then it closed back above the line.

questions.q: Which lesson owns this?
choices: Gap Support, the same trap at one line
A U&R of a swing low
A 2B reversal
A Remount
questions.answer: Gap Support, the same trap at one line
questions.why: Gap Support. The gap-up day's low of a still-open 4% gap on 2x volume is Gap Support, with its own card.
questions.lesson_line: Gap-up day's low, gap still open: that is Gap Support.

wrong.A U&R of a swing low: The level is the gap-up day's low, so the Gap Support card applies.
wrong.A 2B reversal: A 2B fails a swing extreme. This level is a gap low.
wrong.A Remount: A Remount needs a long stay under a line. This was a dip and reclaim.

questions.story: A stock gapped up 6% on earnings on 3x volume. The gap is still open. Days later it dips under the gap-up day's low, then reclaims it.

questions.q: Which setup is this?
choices: A U&R of the 20-day EMA
A 2B of a swing low
An Oops
A spring
questions.answer: A U&R of the 20-day EMA
questions.why: A U&R of the 20-day EMA. A rising 20 EMA is a U&R level; one swing low on its first break is the 2B.
questions.lesson_line: Name the level. A rising average is a U&R. One swing low is a 2B.

wrong.A 2B of a swing low: A 2B is one swing low, on its first break. A rising average is a U&R level.
wrong.An Oops: An Oops needs a gap-open under the prior close and a one-day reclaim.
wrong.A spring: A spring needs a flat range. This level is a rising average.

questions.story: A leader closed above its rising 20-day EMA yesterday. Today it dipped under the line and closed back above it.

questions.q: Which setup is this?
choices: A spring, the Wyckoff cousin
A U&R of a rising average
An Oops
A flat base breakout
questions.answer: A spring, the Wyckoff cousin
questions.why: A spring. It undercuts the floor of a flat range of 15 sessions or more, touched at least twice, and closes back inside by the next day.
questions.lesson_line: Flat range, floor broken, back inside fast: a spring.

wrong.A U&R of a rising average: The level is the floor of a flat range, not a rising average.
wrong.An Oops: An Oops is a one-day gap-open reversal. This follows a range of 20 sessions.
wrong.A flat base breakout: A flat base breakout trades through a ceiling. This broke a floor.

questions.story: A stock sat in a flat range for 20 sessions and touched the floor three times. It broke the floor and closed back inside the next day.

questions.q: Buy the close?
choices: Pass; more than 4% over the level
Buy; the close is strong
Buy half size
Buy with a stop under the close
questions.answer: Pass; more than 4% over the level
questions.why: Pass. At the buy, price is no more than 4% over the level. After a big reclaim day the close can be well over it.
questions.lesson_line: The buy point is the level. Miss it, and let it go.

wrong.Buy; the close is strong: Strength is not the issue. The close sits well over the level, and we never chase past 4%.
wrong.Buy half size: Half of a chase is still a chase. Chasing costs size, not risk.
wrong.Buy with a stop under the close: The stop belongs under the undercut low. A stop at the close is not the trade.

questions.story: A leader reclaims its 100.00 level and runs to a close at 106.20. You did not buy earlier. The undercut low is 98.40.

questions.q: A U&R is a good trade because most of them work.
questions.answer: False
questions.why: False. Most hits are stopped. Even the best-looking reclaim loses about 58% of the time in our scan; the edge is the R of the winners.
questions.lesson_line: The edge is the size of the winners, not the hit rate.

questions.q: What is the call?
choices: Skip it, or size down hard
Take full size; it reclaimed
Move the stop in to 3% and size up
Buy the close, it is a leader
questions.answer: Skip it, or size down hard
questions.why: Skip it, or size down hard. A stop more than about 3% from the entry means size down or skip. This one sat 8.08% away.
questions.lesson_line: A stop that wide breaks the size. Skip or size way down.

wrong.Take full size; it reclaimed: The reclaim passed. The stop distance does not fit, and the size comes from the stop.
wrong.Move the stop in to 3% and size up: Never move the stop in to make it fit. A stop that is not honest is not a stop.
wrong.Buy the close, it is a leader: Buying later does not shrink the stop. It only lets the risk grow.

questions.story: The undercut went to 152.00, 6.88% under the 163.23 level, and the stock closed back above on day two. The stop would sit 8.08% below the buy.

questions.q: Which entry fits our stop rule?
choices: The level entry; the close sizes down
The close entry; it is confirmed
Both fit; the level is the same
Neither; wait a day
questions.answer: The level entry; the close sizes down
questions.why: The level entry. A stop 3% or less from the buy grades well; over 3% means size down, and 6.9% is far over.
questions.lesson_line: The entry near the level keeps the stop small. The late close does not.

wrong.The close entry; it is confirmed: Confirmed or not, 6.9% is far past about 3%. Size down or skip.
wrong.Both fit; the level is the same: The level is the same, but the stop distance is not. The buy price moves the stop width.
wrong.Neither; wait a day: The level entry already fits, with a stop of 1.8%.

questions.story: Same U&R, two entries. Buy the reclaim at the level with a 1.8% stop, or buy the close of the day with a 6.9% stop.

questions.q: How do you treat it?
choices: Take it, graded down for the report
Pass; the report is too close
Take it at full size, the report is far
Wait until after the report
questions.answer: Take it, graded down for the report
questions.why: Take it, graded down. A report within a week is a B minus cue. The hard line is a report inside 3 sessions.
questions.lesson_line: Three sessions is the wall. Inside a week is a lower grade.

wrong.Pass; the report is too close: The hard line is a report inside 3 sessions. Five sessions out is allowed, at a lower grade.
wrong.Take it at full size, the report is far: A report within a week is a B minus cue. It trims the grade, so it trims the size.
wrong.Wait until after the report: Nothing in the rules forces a wait at five sessions.

questions.story: A perfect U&R triggers. The next earnings report is five sessions away. Nothing else is pending.

questions.q: How do you file this trade?
choices: A planned loss; the system worked
A mistake; the entry was early
A reason to widen stops next time
A sign to drop the setup
questions.answer: A planned loss; the system worked
questions.why: A planned loss. NVDA reached 0.67R, then was stopped on day 2. The best-looking reclaim still loses most of the time.
questions.lesson_line: Rules followed, stop hit: a planned loss. Next trade.

wrong.A mistake; the entry was early: The entry followed every rule. The stop is the exit, and this was a loss taken at it.
wrong.A reason to widen stops next time: The stop only moves up, never wider. A wider stop would only have made the loss bigger.
wrong.A sign to drop the setup: One stop says nothing. The edge is in the winners over many trades.

questions.story: You bought a U&R at 87.63 with the stop at 85.83. The reclaim day closed in its top half. Two sessions later the stock trades 83.02 and you are stopped.

questions.q: What does this loss teach?
choices: Stop worked; the index had not turned
Never trade a gap up
Hold through a close under the stop
Buy larger next time
questions.answer: Stop worked; the index had not turned
questions.why: The stop worked. ADBE sold off through it the day SPY made a lower low, so the index had not turned.
questions.lesson_line: A clean-looking U&R means little while the index is still falling.

wrong.Never trade a gap up: The gap up was not the problem. The index had not turned.
wrong.Hold through a close under the stop: The stop is a real order and it is the exit.
wrong.Buy larger next time: Larger size on a failed idea is a bigger loss.

questions.story: You bought a U&R at the open, 218.83, with the stop at 214.73. The stock gapped up, sold off all day and closed at 213.80, through the stop.

questions.q: Buy again?
choices: No; a new try needs a new trigger
Yes, it is the same setup
Yes, with a wider stop
Yes, at double size to recover
questions.answer: No; a new try needs a new trigger
questions.why: No. After a stop-out, buy again only on a new trigger, as a new trade. AMD's stop did its job.
questions.lesson_line: A stop-out is not a signal to buy again. Wait for a new trigger.

wrong.Yes, it is the same setup: The same setup is not a trigger. A new try is a new trade with its own trigger and stop.
wrong.Yes, with a wider stop: A wider stop to get back in is the mistake, not the fix.
wrong.Yes, at double size to recover: Doubling to win it back is how a small loss gets bigger. Size comes from the stop.

questions.story: You bought a U&R at 105.52 and were stopped at 102.58. Weeks later the stock is back near 105. Nothing new has triggered.

questions.q: Is the open a valid buy?
choices: Yes; back over the level, within 4%
No; it must close above first
No; a gap means skip
Only if volume doubles
questions.answer: Yes; back over the level, within 4%
questions.why: Yes. Two closes under is inside the window, and the open is back over the level and well inside 4%. WYNN bought the open, 0.4% over.
questions.lesson_line: A gap back over the level is the reclaim. Buy it at the open.

wrong.No; it must close above first: The trigger is the trade back above the level. We do not wait for the close.
wrong.No; a gap means skip: A gap back over the level is allowed. WYNN did it and the open was only 0.4% over.
wrong.Only if volume doubles: A volume surge is not the trigger. The trade back over the level is.

questions.story: The level is 159.37. The stock closed under it two days running. The next morning it opens at 159.97.

questions.q: Hidden ticker, the reclaim day. A low just undercut a level and closed back above it. Is the 50-day rising? Take it or pass?
choices: Take it; the 50-day is rising
Pass; the 50-day is falling
Pass; the undercut is too small
questions.answer: Take it; the 50-day is rising
questions.why: Take it. A two-week shelf above a rising 50-day, one poke under the level, then a reclaim that closes near the high. It ran 31.4R.
questions.lesson_line: Rising 50-day, shallow undercut, quick reclaim: that is the trade.

wrong.Pass; the 50-day is falling: Look again: the 50-day runs up under the shelf.
wrong.Pass; the undercut is too small: A shallow undercut is the point. The 1.39% dip was a clean one.

questions.q: Hidden ticker, the reclaim day. A level was undercut and taken back the same day. Where is the close against the 200-day? Take it or pass?
choices: Pass; under a falling 200-day
Take it; the reclaim was the same day
Take it; the undercut was shallow
questions.answer: Pass; under a falling 200-day
questions.why: Pass. The close was 9.7% under a falling 200-day SMA. No longs below the 200-day is a hard rule.
questions.lesson_line: A U&R shape under the 200-day is a watch, not a buy.

wrong.Take it; the reclaim was the same day: A same-day reclaim is the best shape, but the context fails first.
wrong.Take it; the undercut was shallow: The undercut was shallow, and the 200-day still says no.

questions.q: Take the fourth try?
choices: No; the limit is 3 a week
Yes, it is a new trigger
Yes, at half size
Yes, if the stop is tight
questions.answer: No; the limit is 3 a week
questions.why: No. A new try needs a new trigger, and it is at most 3 a week and 6 a month on one stock.
questions.lesson_line: Three tries a week on one stock. Then you walk away.

wrong.Yes, it is a new trigger: A new trigger is needed, but it is not enough. The cap is 3 tries a week on one stock.
wrong.Yes, at half size: Half size does not lift the cap.
wrong.Yes, if the stop is tight: A tight stop does not lift the cap.

questions.story: You were stopped three times on this stock this week, each on its own trigger. A fourth U&R trigger appears on Friday.

questions.q: Account 100,000, risk 0.25%. Buy 245.39, stop 235.64. How many shares does the stop allow?
questions.why: 25 shares. The size comes from the stop: risk divided by the distance, rounded down. That stop was 3.97% from the buy, so LULU sized small.
questions.lesson_line: The size comes from the stop. A wide stop means few shares.
